**Refined prompt:** Answer from the actual slug-generation code whether two articles with identical titles can end up with the same slug — covering both the create path and any other write path that sets `slug`, what enforcement exists at the DB level, and what a collision would actually break. Cite file:line.

## On create: no — but only probabilistically

`src/article/article.service.ts:201-203`:

```ts
slugify(title: string) {
  return slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + (Math.random() * Math.pow(36, 6) | 0).toString(36)
}
```

Same title → same base, but a random base-36 suffix is appended. Two people publishing "How to Train Your Dragon" get `how-to-train-your-dragon-k3n1qr` and `how-to-train-your-dragon-8vz0p2`.

The suffix space is 36⁶ = 2,176,782,336 (~31 bits). Birthday bound within one same-title group: two articles ≈ 4.6 × 10⁻¹⁰; 1,000 articles ≈ 0.02%; you need ~55,000 articles sharing a title for a coin-flip. Not a practical worry.

**But nothing enforces it.** `article.entity.ts:11-12` is a bare `@Column() slug: string` — no unique index (confirmed in `.claude/knowledge/schema.md:31`). If the draw ever repeats, the insert succeeds silently.

## The real collision vector is `PUT`, not `POST`

`article.service.ts:190-195`:

```ts
async update(slug: string, articleData: any): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  let toUpdate = await this.articleRepository.findOne({ slug: slug});
  let updated = Object.assign(toUpdate, articleData);
```

`articleData` is `any`, it's `Object.assign`'d wholesale, and `ArticleController.update()` (`article.controller.ts:59-63`) has **no validation pipe** — the only `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())` in the codebase are on `UserController` (`user.controller.ts:31,42`). So:

```
PUT /api/articles/some-article-abc123
{"article": {"slug": "someone-elses-article-xyz789"}}
```

writes that slug directly. Deterministic collision, no DB constraint to stop it. And `update()` never compares `req.user.id` to `article.author.id`, so any authenticated user can do this to anyone's article — the `403 Forbidden` on line 58 is annotation only. (Both halves of this are already in `LESSONS.md` — #112 on `Object.assign`, #6/#44 on auth ≠ authz.)

## What a collision costs you

Every slug lookup is `findOne({slug})` — lines 102, 115, 132, 148, 166, 191. `findOne` returns one row, so the loser becomes unreachable: can't be fetched, commented on, or favorited.

Worse, `article.service.ts:197-198`:

```ts
async delete(slug: string): Promise<DeleteResult> {
  return await this.articleRepository.delete({ slug: slug});
}
```

That's a delete-by-criteria, not by id — `DELETE FROM article WHERE slug = ?` removes **every** row with that slug. Deleting your own article takes the colliding one with it.

## Related, since you're in this area

`article.controller.ts:61` — `// Todo: update slug also when title gets changed`. Changing a title leaves the old slug, so the two drift apart permanently.

**Not read:** I didn't run anything or check tests, and I didn't verify `slug@^1.1.0`'s transliteration behavior for unicode or punctuation-only titles.

One incidental bug I noticed while reading the suffix: `| 0` is ToInt32, and 36⁶ (2,176,782,336) exceeds 2³¹. About 1.35% of draws wrap negative, producing slugs like `my-title--1x2y3z` — a leading minus and a double hyphen. Harmless for uniqueness, ugly in URLs. `Math.floor()` instead of `| 0` fixes it.
